Tests must be red now (no implementation exists) and must never be deleted or weakened afterwards: gate 2 ratchets test count across this and earlier stages. --- # STAGE 1 REQUIREMENTS (R-1-001 … R-1-244) Source of truth: `/home/prashant/projects/dark-factory-wearedevs/pocketful/spec/stage-1.md`. `§` refs are to that file. ## A. Invariants — hold at every read, under concurrency and retries - **R-1-001** The sum of all wallet balances always equals the sum of the `balance` values seeded by the last successful `POST /_test/reset` (or restored by `POST /_test/import`), at every read, after any mix of concurrent payments, request payments, splits, settlements and replays. (§1.1, §9) [invariant] - **R-1-002** No wallet balance is ever negative, not even transiently: no observable read and no intermediate state inside any operation leaves a balance below zero. (§1.2) [invariant] - **R-1-003** A payment request moves money at most once: a replayed write returns the original response and makes no further state change. (§1.3, §7) [invariant] - **R-1-004** Every amount in the API and in storage is an exact integer count of minor units; no floating-point rounding error is ever observable, and split shares sum exactly to the split `amount`. (§4, §9) [invariant] - **R-1-005** No request produces a 5xx response, including under 50 concurrent in-flight requests. (§5) [invariant] - **R-1-006** Concurrent requests produce results equal to executing them one at a time in some order (serializable); the debit and credit of a payment are one atomic step, never visible in one wallet and not the other, and a failed payment leaves no trace in either wallet. (§8) [invariant] - **R-1-007** A rejected write (any 4xx) changes no balance, creates no payment, no request and no settlement, and leaves no record other than those the idempotency rules require. (§5, §7, §11) [invariant] ## B. Delivery and deployment - **R-1-010** The stage folder contains a `Dockerfile` that builds the service with no manual setup, and a `RUN.md` giving the exact build-and-start command. (§2) - **R-1-011** The image runs standalone with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping; no compose file, external service, volume or sidecar is needed to start or serve. (§2) - **R-1-012** The service listens on `0.0.0.0` on the port given by the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `8080` when `PORT` is unset. (§3.1) - **R-1-013** The container makes no outbound network request at run time; all dependencies, fonts, scripts, stylesheets and seed data are baked into the image during build. (§2) - **R-1-014** `GET /health` returns `200` with body `{"status": "ok"}` once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 s of container start. Non-200 before readiness is permitted. (§3.2) - **R-1-015** The service stays correct and responsive within 2 vCPU and 2 GiB with up to 50 requests in flight; every request other than the test-control endpoints completes within 5 s, and `POST /_test/reset`, `POST /_test/import` and `GET /_test/export` within 10 s. (§2, §10) [limit] - **R-1-016** Service state need not survive a container restart; no on-disk durability is required. (§2) ## C. Conventions - **R-1-020** Every JSON response carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and request bodies are read as UTF-8 JSON. (§3.4) - **R-1-021** Every timestamp in a response is RFC 3339 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+00:00`); a bare local time or a naive offset-less form is never emitted. (§3.4) - **R-1-022** Unknown fields in any request body are ignored and are never an error. (§3.4) - **R-1-023** Unknown query parameters on any endpoint are ignored and are never an error. (§3.4) - **R-1-024** Every id the service assigns is an opaque string of at most 64 characters; format is the implementation's choice but ids are unique within their kind for the life of a reset. (§3.4) - **R-1-025** Seeded ids supplied in a fixture are used verbatim as the service's ids for those users, payments and requests, and are returned unchanged by the API. (§4) ## D. Model: currency, users, handles - **R-1-030** The service has exactly one currency and one `minor_units` value, both declared by the fixture; `minor_units` is `0`, `2` or `3`, and fixtures use `EUR` (2), `JPY` (0) and `BHD` (3). (§4) - **R-1-031** Every API `amount` is an integer count of minor units; JSON `1000`, `1000.0` and `1e3` are all accepted as the same valid amount because their numeric value is integral. (§4) - **R-1-032** A JSON boolean or string in an `amount` field is not a number and is rejected with `422 validation_failed` (not `400`). (§4, §5) - **R-1-033** A numeric `amount` with a non-integral value (e.g. `10.5`, `1e-1`) is `422 validation_failed`. (§8) - **R-1-034** Every user has a handle that is unique across the service, matches `^[a-z0-9_]{1,20}$`, and never changes once set. (§4) - **R-1-035** Recipients and payers are identified in request bodies by handle only; no directory or user-search endpoint exists. (§4) - **R-1-036** A user created through `POST /auth/signup` gets a handle derived from the email: take the local part (everything before the first `@`), lowercase it, replace every character outside `[a-z0-9_]` with `_`, then truncate to 20 characters. (§4, §6) - **R-1-037** A newly signed-up user starts with balance `0`, can immediately receive money and can immediately be asked for money. (§4) ## E. Fixture, reset, and seeding - **R-1-040** `POST /_test/reset` with a fixture body replaces **all** service state and returns `204 No Content`; after it returns, every subsequent request sees only that fixture and nothing from before it. (§3.3) - **R-1-041** `POST /_test/reset` requires no authentication, is enabled in the delivered image, and may be called repeatedly; each call fully replaces the previous state. (§3.3) - **R-1-042** A reset fixture seeds `currency`, `minor_units`, `users` (`id`, `email`, `password`, `display_name`, `handle`, `balance`), optional `payments` (`id`, `from_user_id`, `to_user_id`, `amount`, `note`, `visibility`), optional `requests` (`id`, `requester_id`, `payer_id`, `amount`, `note`, `status`) and optional `settlement_operator_ids` (default `[]`). (§4, §11) - **R-1-043** A seeded user's `balance` is the wallet balance **after** every seeded payment; seeded payments are **not** replayed against balances, so loading them leaves the seeded balance unchanged. (§4) - **R-1-044** Seeded users can log in with the seeded plaintext `password` immediately after reset. (§4) - **R-1-045** A fixture containing any `balance` below zero makes `POST /_test/reset` return `422 validation_failed` and change nothing (the prior state remains fully intact and servable). (§4) - **R-1-046** A reset body that does not parse as JSON, or whose top level is not a JSON object, is `400 malformed_request` and changes nothing. (§4, §5) - **R-1-048** Any field the fixture does not mention is ignored, and a fixture omitting `payments`, `requests` or `settlement_operator_ids` is valid; the omitted collection is empty. (§3.4, §4, §11) - **R-1-049** Seeded requests keep their seeded `status`; a seeded non-`pending` request is not payable and a seeded `pending` request is payable exactly like an API-created one. (§4, §8) - **R-1-050** There is no administrative balance endpoint, and no endpoint other than reset/import may set a balance directly. (§4) ## F. Errors and precedence - **R-1-060** Every 4xx and 5xx response body is exactly `{"error": {"code": "<code>", "message": "<any wording>"}}` with the specified status and code; `message` wording is free but must be a non-empty string. (§5) - **R-1-061** `400 malformed_request`: the body does not parse as JSON, the top level is not a JSON object, or a field is of the wrong JSON type and no endpoint-specific rule overrides it. (§5) - **R-1-062** `400 missing_idempotency_key`: a required `Idempotency-Key` header is absent or empty. (§5, §7) - **R-1-063** `401 unauthenticated`: the `Authorization` header is missing, not of the form `Bearer <token>`, or carries an unknown token. (§5, §6) - **R-1-064** `403 forbidden`: the caller is authenticated but not permitted to act on this resource. (§5) - **R-1-065** `404 not_found`: no such resource, or the resource is not visible to this caller. (§5) - **R-1-066** `409 idempotency_key_reuse`: the key was already used by this caller with a different request body on the same method and path. (§5, §7) - **R-1-067** `422 validation_failed`: a required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated and no more specific code applies. (§5) - **R-1-068** A field of the **correct** JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value is `422 validation_failed` unless the endpoint names a different code; this covers invalid instants, negative counts and values over a stated maximum or length. (§5) - **R-1-069** Endpoint field rules take precedence over the wrong-type rule for three fields: an invalid `amount` (including a string or boolean), a non-string `note` (including `null`), and any `visibility` other than `"public"` or `"private"` are all `422 validation_failed`, never `400`. (§5) - **R-1-070** Omitting an optional field selects its default and is never an error; omitting a required field is `422 validation_failed`. (§5) - **R-1-071** An integer-valued **query parameter** must be written as plain decimal digits; `1e9`, `4.0`, `+4`, ` 4`, `0x4` and an empty value are `422 validation_failed` whatever their numeric value. (§5) - **R-1-072** `Idempotency-Key` must be 1 to 255 characters: longer than 255 is `422 validation_failed`; absent or empty is `400 missing_idempotency_key`. (§5, §7) - **R-1-073** `limit` is an integer 1 to 200; anything else (including `0`, `201`, negative or non-digit forms) is `422 validation_failed`. (§5, §8) - **R-1-074** `offset` is an integer 0 or more; anything else is `422 validation_failed`. (§5, §8) - **R-1-075** **PLANNER DECISION (ambiguity resolved).** Error precedence on every endpoint is, in order: (1) `401 unauthenticated`; (2) endpoint-level permission not depending on the body (`403 forbidden` for a non-operator on `POST /settlements`); (3) `400 malformed_request` for an unparseable or non-object body; (4) `400 missing_idempotency_key`; (5) `422 validation_failed` for an over-long `Idempotency-Key`; (6) idempotency resolution (`200` replay or `409 idempotency_key_reuse`); (7) endpoint field validation (`422`, including `self_payment` / `self_request`); (8) resource lookup (`404 not_found`); (9) permission on the looked-up resource (`403 forbidden`); (10) resource-state checks (`409 request_not_pending`); (11) funds (`409 insufficient_funds`). (§5, §7, §8, §11) - **R-1-076** **PLANNER DECISION.** Within step (7) of R-1-075, body fields are validated in this fixed order so the returned code is deterministic: required-field presence → wrong-type fields → `amount` range and integrality → `note` length → `visibility` value → handle syntax → duplicate/empty collection rules → self-reference (`self_payment` / `self_request`). (§5) - **R-1-077** **PLANNER DECISION.** A `to_handle`, `payer_handle` or participant handle that is a string but does not match `^[a-z0-9_]{1,20}$` is `422 validation_failed` (R-1-068); a syntactically valid handle with no such user is `404 not_found`. A non-string handle is `400 malformed_request`. (§4, §5) - **R-1-078** A 4xx response never leaks a resource the caller may not see: a request or payment the caller is not party to is reported with the same code and body as a nonexistent one, except where the spec names `403 forbidden`. Export and import - **R-1-200** `GET /_test/export` is unauthenticated and returns `200` with a JSON object containing `track: "pocketful"`, `format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). (§10) - **R-1-201** `POST /_test/import` is unauthenticated, takes that entire object, atomically replaces all service state, and returns `204`. (§10) - **R-1-202** Import accepts an unchanged export produced by this service with no dependency on the source process, files, volume, port or network address. (§10) - **R-1-203** Import is replacement, not merge: it removes all previous destination data and credentials, and repeating the same import restores the same state without duplicating anything. (§10) - **R-1-204** An import body that does not parse is `400 malformed_request`; a missing field, a `track` other than `pocketful`, a `format_version` other than `1`, or an invalid `state` is `422 validation_failed`; in every failure case the destination state is unchanged. (§10, §5) - **R-1-205** Export/import preserves accounts and hashed-password login, every existing bearer token, the currency and `minor_units`, all balances, all payments, all requests with their statuses, settlement operator permissions and settlement membership. (§10, §11) - **R-1-206** Export/import preserves every completed idempotent request body together with its original response status and body, so a retry after import returns the original response (`200` with the original body); keys whose original request failed with 4xx remain reusable after import. (§10) - **R-1-207** Import regenerates no identity, timestamp or monetary record, and never replays seeded or exported payments against an already-net balance; balances after import equal balances at export exactly. (§10) [invariant] - **R-1-208** Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot: writes on the source after the export returns do not change the exported document, and export changes no state. (§10) - **R-1-209** `POST /_test/reset` clears all state including imported state. (§10) - **R-1-210** Replacing destination state with a fresh fixture does not satisfy import: receipts, tokens and retry identity carried in the export must be live in the destination. (§10) ## O. Atomic net settlements - **R-1-220** The fixture field `settlement_operator_ids` is an array of user ids defaulting to `[]`; those users are settlement operators. (§11) - **R-1-221** `POST /settlements` requires an idempotency key and a settlement operator: no/unknown token is `401 unauthenticated`; an authenticated non-operator is `403 forbidden`. (§11) - **R-1-222** Operator permission grants only settlement execution: it gives no access to another user's requests and no visibility of another user's `private` activity items. (§11) - **R-1-223** The body is `{"transfers":[{"from_handle","to_handle","amount","note","visibility"}…]}` with 1 to 32 entries; each entry follows ordinary payment `amount`, `note` and `visibility` rules, defaulting to empty note and `public`. (§11) - **R-1-224** A malformed batch shape — `transfers` absent, not an array, empty, or longer than 32 — is `422 validation_failed` (not `400`). (§11) - **R-1-226** Entry errors take precedence in input order — the first entry with any error determines the response — and all entry errors take precedence over `409 insufficient_funds`. (§11) - **R-1-228** Either all movements of a settlement commit together or none do; no intermediate state is observable in which some transfers are applied. (§11) [invariant] - **R-1-229** A settlement that fails validation or affordability claims no idempotency key and creates no payment and no revision. (§11) - **R-1-231** Every settlement member is an ordinary payment carrying `settlement_id` linking the batch, `request_id: null`, and a server-assigned `created_at` identical for all members and equal to `committed_at`. (§11) - **R-1-232** Payments outside a settlement expose `settlement_id: null`. (§11) - **R-1-233** Replaying a settlement returns `200` with the original complete response and moves no money; `POST /settlements` is the fifth idempotent write path. (§11) - **R-1-234** Unknown fields inside `transfers` entries and in the settlement body are ignored. (§11, §3.4) - **R-1-235** A reset or import preserves settlement operator permissions, the original settlement payments, settlement membership and settlement retry responses. (§11, §10) - **R-1-236** **PLANNER DECISION.** A settlement entry whose `from_handle` or `to_handle` is the operator's own handle is permitted; the `self_payment` rule applies only within one entry (`from_handle == to_handle`). (§1, §5) [invariant] - **R-1-241** Two concurrent pays of the same `pending` request by the payer with **different** keys result in exactly one `201` payment and one `409 request_not_pending`; money moves once. (§8) [invariant] - **R-1-242** Two concurrent payments from the same wallet that together exceed its balance cannot both succeed; at least one returns `409 insufficient_funds`. The same key with the same body on a **different path** is a different request and must succeed normally. - **R-1-103** First use of a key returns the endpoint's normal success status, `201`. - **R-1-104** A replay returns `200` with a body identical to the original response **as a JSON value**. - **R-1-105** The same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse` and changes nothing. - **R-1-106** "Same body" is the same JSON value after parsing: key order and whitespace do not matter. **Numbers compare by exact numeric value**, so `1000`, `1000.0` and `1e3` in the same field *are* the same body. An **absent** key versus that key **present with its default value** are **different** bodies — so `{}` and `{"visibility":"public"}` are different, and reusing one key across them is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`. - **R-1-107** A key reused after the original request failed with **any** 4xx is treated as a first use and may succeed. - **R-1-108** For N concurrent identical requests with an unused key, **exactly one** returns `201` and the rest return `200` with the identical body. The operation takes effect exactly once. - **R-1-109** A successful replay returns the original response even after the underlying resource has changed, been paid, declined or cancelled, and makes no further state change. - **R-1-110** Once the body has parsed as a JSON object and the caller is authenticated, a claimed key is resolved **before** endpoint field validation and before any current-resource check. A replay of a key claimed under an earlier stage's schema returns exactly that earlier body, without any field a later stage added to the resource (no `authorization_id`, no `refund_of`). This is what makes R-1-104 and R-1-206 hold across an upgrade. - **R-1-072** `Idempotency-Key` 1..255 characters: over 255 is `422 validation_failed`; absent or empty is `400 missing_idempotency_key`. - **R-1-075** steps (4)(5)(6): missing key → key length → idempotency resolution, all **before** field validation, lookup, resource permission, state and funds. ## The hard parts — work these out explicitly **R-1-108 is the one that bites.** A losing racer must **not** get `409`, and must not get an error: it has to end up returning `200` with the winner's stored body. Three states, not two — a key is *unclaimed*, *in flight*, or *complete*. A racer that finds the key in flight must wait for the winner to finish and then return its stored response. If you implement "claim or 409" you will pass every sequential test and fail the storm, which sends 300 replays at 50-way concurrency. Claim the key and run the operation under the **same** serialization point you already use for funds, so "in flight" is never observable as a gap. **R-1-112 vs R-1-104 is a trap for later stages.** Store the serialized response body at the moment you produce it and return those bytes (or that exact parsed value) on replay. Key scoping is (user, method, path, key) — not (user, key). Same key, same body, different path → both succeed (R-1-102). Same key on `POST /payments` and `POST /requests` are unrelated records. 2. Path identity for parameterised paths is the **concrete** path: `POST /requests/rq_1/pay` and `POST /requests/rq_2/pay` with the same key and the same body `{}` are different paths, so both succeed. 3. Two users, same key string, same path, different bodies → both `201`, no interference (R-1-101). 4. `409 idempotency_key_reuse` must not consume or alter the original record: after it, replaying the *original* body still returns `200` with the original response. 5. A replay must return `200` even when the original returned `201` — the status differs, the body does not. 6. Body equality must ignore key order *recursively*, including inside `transfers` entries and `participant_handles` — but **array order is significant** (`["ada","bob"]` ≠ `["bob","ada"]`, and they genuinely produce different splits). 7. Unknown fields are ignored for *validation* (R-1-022) but they are part of the **body** for equality: `{"amount":1}` and `{"amount":1,"zz":2}` are different JSON values, so the same key across them is `409`. Do not strip unknown fields before hashing. 8. An over-255-character key is `422` and claims nothing, so the same (shortened) key is still unused afterwards. 9. A key whose original request 4xx'd is reusable even with a *different* body (R-1-107 — it was never claimed). 10. `POST /requests/{id}/decline` and `/cancel` take **no** key (R-1-100): sending `Idempotency-Key` on them is ignored, never an error, and never stored. ## Handoff Commit with the pathspec form; `git status --porcelain` first. Mind one more trap while you are in there: `float('nan') != float('nan')`, so a body containing `NaN` would never replay. Fixed with `_end_headers_with_body()`: appends the blank-line terminator and the body to the **same** `_headers_buffer` the stdlib already accumulates headers into, then issues **one** `wfile.write()` for the whole response. Replaces `end_headers()` + a trailing body write in `send_error`, `_write_json`, and `do_OPTIONS` — every response path now writes in one shot. The drain-before-close fix from `c552f89` stays; it's a separate, still-real risk (RST discarding an already-sent response when unread input remains on close) and the two fixes are complementary. ## The 50-iteration evidence, against the real fix Started the actual service as a separate process, ran both relevant tests 50 times each via direct subprocess calls to pytest: - `test_over_long_header_block_400`: **50/50 passed, zero failures** - `test_over_long_request_line_400`: **50/50 passed, zero failures** ## Gate 2, once, with `--commit` ``` .venv/bin/python -m factory.gates.run stage-1 --gates 2 --commit 639e71a ``` **314 passed, 0 failed** — exactly as expected.

the payer's `total` falls by the captured amount and the receiver's rises by it. - **R-2-056** With `final` true (the default) the authorization becomes `captured`, carries cumulative `captured_amount` and `payment_id`, and **releases the uncaptured remainder immediately** — capturing 1500 of 2000 returns 500 to the payer's `available` in the same step. `remaining_amount` becomes `0` and `closed_at` is set. - **R-2-057** A second capture after a final capture is `409 authorization_not_open`. - **R-2-058** With `final: false` and a nonzero uncaptured remainder, `status` stays `open`, the remainder stays held, and further captures are allowed up to that remainder. - **R-2-059** Capturing the entire remainder closes the authorization (`status: "captured"`, `remaining_amount: 0`) even with `final: false`. - **R-2-060** `422 capture_exceeds_authorization` compares `amount` with the **remaining** amount, not the original amount; an omitted `amount` defaults to that remainder and therefore never triggers it. - **R-2-061** `captured_amount` is cumulative across captures; `payment_id` is the latest capture; `payment_ids` lists every capture in order; `remaining_amount` is the amount still held and is `0` when closed. - **R-2-062** Void and expiry can close a partially captured authorization, release only the remainder, and preserve all capture records. - **R-2-063** The new fields (`final`, `remaining_amount`, `payment_ids`, `closed_at`) do not change idempotency body equality: equality is still the parsed JSON value of the request body (R-1-106). - **R-2-064** Capture errors and their precedence: unknown authorization → `404 not_found`; caller not the receiver → `403 forbidden`; `expires_at` at or before now → `409 authorization_expired`; status not `open` → `409 authorization_not_open`; `amount` above the remainder → `422 capture_exceeds_authorization`; `amount` below 1 or non-integral, or `final` not boolean → `422 validation_failed`. Field validation precedes lookup per R-1-075; `capture_exceeds_authorization` is evaluated after the state checks because it needs the remainder. - **R-2-065** **Decision.** When an authorization is both expired by the clock and not `open` by status, `409 authorization_expired` wins for a seeded/API `open` authorization past its deadline, and `409 authorization_not_open` wins for one already `captured` or `voided`. - **R-2-066** A capture whose money is already reserved **never fails for funds**: the hold guarantees the payer can pay, so a capture within the remainder never returns `409 insufficient_funds` even if the payer's `available` is zero. **Void — `POST /authorizations/{id}/void`** - **R-2-070** Takes no idempotency key and may be called **only by the payer** (the `from` party), releasing their own hold. - **R-2-071** Success is `200` with the authorization at `status: "voided"`, the hold released, `remaining_amount: 0` and `closed_at` set; `available` rises by the released remainder in the same step. - **R-2-072** Voiding an already-`voided` authorization is `200` with the current state and releases nothing further. - **R-2-073** Voiding a `captured` or `expired` authorization is `409 authorization_not_open`. - **R-2-074** For an existing authorization, capture and void return `403 forbidden` when the caller is not the permitted party, including callers who are neither party; an unknown id is `404 not_found`. - **R-2-075** Void moves no money and changes no `total`. **Invariants this item must not break:** R-2-003 (cumulative captures never exceed the authorized amount; each idempotent capture moves money once; a closed hold can never be captured again), R-2-005 (a hold is released exactly once — by final capture, void, or expiry — so no wallet's `available` ever exceeds its `total`), R-2-181/182 (concurrent captures, and capture racing void, produce exactly one winner), plus R-1-001/002/003. ## Three traps specific to this item 1. **R-2-066 vs R-2-002 is the subtle one.** Held money is unavailable to *new* spending but **is** available to the capture it was reserved for. If you implement the capture debit as an ordinary funds check against `available`, every capture of a fully-held wallet fails and R-2-066 breaks. The capture spends from the hold, not from `available`. 2. **R-2-005 is where double-release lives.** Final capture, void and expiry each release the remainder. A partial capture followed by a void must release *only* what is left (R-2-062), and expiry of an already-closed hold must release nothing. Any path that releases twice makes `available` exceed `total` — that is money created from nothing, and @adversary will go straight at it. 3. **R-2-065's precedence collision.** Expired-and-open → `authorization_expired`; already-captured-or-voided → `authorization_not_open`. This is the other feature stage 3 is actually about, and **15 of the 29 remaining red tests are yours**, the largest block left in the stage. ### Requirements, pasted in full - **R-3-050** `POST /payments/{payment_id}/corrections` requires an `Idempotency-Key` and the **original sender**. It is the eighth idempotent write path. - **R-3-051** An authenticated non-sender is `403 forbidden`; an unknown payment is `404 not_found`; no token is `401 unauthenticated`. - **R-3-052** The body is `{"expected_revision", "amount", "effective_at", "reason"}` and **all four fields are required**; omitting any is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-3-053** `expected_revision` is a positive integer; `amount` is an integer `0..1000000000` (zero reverses the entire payment); `reason` is a string of 1..200 characters; `effective_at` is an RFC 3339 instant **not later than now**. Any violation is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-3-054** A correction changes neither the parties nor the visibility of the payment. - **R-3-055** Success appends an **immutable** revision and returns `201` with `{"payment_id", "revision", "amount", "effective_at", "recorded_at", "reason"}`, `recorded_at` server-assigned. - **R-3-056** An `expected_revision` that is not the payment's current latest revision is `409 stale_revision`, changing nothing. - **R-3-057** A successful replay returns `200` with **that original revision**, even after newer revisions exist; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`. - **R-3-058** The difference from the previous amount moves between the **same two wallets** in the same atomic step: increasing the amount debits the original sender, decreasing it debits the original receiver. - **R-3-059** A currently unaffordable debit is `409 insufficient_funds`. **Current unaffordability takes precedence over historical overdraft.** - **R-3-060** Otherwise, if any user's corrected balance would be negative at **any** effective-time boundary, it is `409 historical_overdraft`. Balances at a boundary include the combined effect of all movements at that instant. - **R-3-061** Either failure preserves balances, revision history, statements and idempotency state exactly; a rejected correction **claims no key**. - **R-3-062** The original payment and every original idempotent response remain unchanged; `GET /activity` continues to display the original payment, and correction records are never new feed payments. - **R-3-063** `GET /payments/{payment_id}/revisions` returns `{"revisions": [...]}` in revision order, **including revision 1** with `reason: ""`. - **R-3-064** Only the two parties may read a payment's revisions; a third party gets `404 not_found` **even for a public payment**; no token is `401 unauthenticated`. - **R-3-065** A correction of a **settlement member** is `422 linked_payment_immutable`. - **R-3-066** A correction of a **capture** is `422 linked_payment_immutable`. - **R-3-067** Concurrent corrections using the same `expected_revision` cannot both succeed: exactly one returns `201`, the other `409 stale_revision`. - **R-3-068** *(planner decision)* Precedence, extending R-1-075: `401` → `404 not_found` (unknown payment) → `403 forbidden` (non-sender) → `400 missing_idempotency_key` → idempotency resolution → `422 validation_failed` (field rules) → `422 linked_payment_immutable` → `409 stale_revision` → `409 insufficient_funds` → `409 historical_overdraft`. **Immutability precedes staleness** because a capture or settlement member can never be corrected at any revision. - **R-3-069** *(planner decision)* A correction whose `amount` equals the current amount is **valid, not a no-op error**: it appends a revision with a zero movement. Also binding and already built: **R-3-055's recorded times strictly increase** per payment (R-3-010 family), and the four invariants — conservation (R-3-001/R-1-001), no negative balance (R-1-002), money moves at most once (R-1-003), exact integers (R-1-004).
